items.front: Who founded the Mauryan empire, when, and with whose help?
items.back: Chandragupta Maurya, 322 BCE, guided by Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: What did the Chandragupta–Seleucus treaty (305 BCE) give?
items.back: NW areas (Kabul/Kandahar/Herat/Baluchistan) + marriage; 500 elephants to Seleucus; Megasthenes sent.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Megasthenes' account of Mauryan India is called?
items.back: Indica.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Chanakya's treatise and its key ideas?
items.back: Arthashastra — Saptanga theory, Mantriparishad, espionage, Yogakshema.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Bindusara's title and Greek envoys to his court?
items.back: 'Amitraghata'; envoys Deimachus (Antiochus I) and Dionysius.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: In which year was the Kalinga War, and its edict?
items.back: 261 BCE; described in Major Rock Edict 13 (bherighosha → dhammaghosha).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: What names do inscriptions use for Ashoka?
items.back: Devanampiya Piyadasi; name 'Ashoka' confirmed by Maski/Gujarra/Nettur edicts.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Scripts used in Ashoka's edicts?
items.back: Brahmi (most), Kharosthi (NW), Greek & Aramaic (Afghanistan/Kandahar).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Which Andhra Pradesh site has Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts?
items.back: Erragudi (Yerragudi).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Where was the 'Ranyo Ashoka' portrait-inscription found?
items.back: Kanganahalli (Sannati), Karnataka.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Third Buddhist Council — venue, patron, president?
items.back: Pataliputra, under Ashoka, presided by Moggaliputta Tissa; sent missions (Mahinda/Sanghamitra).
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Ashoka's most famous art work; national emblem?
items.back: Sarnath Lion Capital — India's national emblem.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Key Mauryan provincial officials?
items.back: Kumaras (viceroys) at Taxila/Ujjain/Suvarnagiri/Tosali; Rajukas, Yuktas, Pradeshikas.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: Who ended the Mauryan empire and when?
items.back: General Pushyamitra Shunga killed last Maurya Brihadratha, 185 BCE.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History

items.front: What does Brahmanical tradition say about Chandragupta’s birth?
items.back: That he was born of a shudra woman at the Nanda court.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: Which eastern regions lay in Chandragupta’s empire?
items.back: Bihar, Orissa and Bengal, besides the north and north-west.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: What kind of ruler was Chandragupta Maurya?
items.back: An autocrat who kept all powers in his own hands.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: What was achieved for the first time in Indian history under the Mauryas?
items.back: Political unification of most of the country under one centralised empire.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: What happened to republics under the Mauryas?
items.back: Republican and oligarchic government came to an end; monarchy reached its height.

items.front: Mauryan capital and its modern name?
items.back: Pataliputra — present-day Patna.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: To which archaeological age does the Mauryan Empire belong?
items.back: The Iron Age.
items.source: APPSC GK — Ancient History: The Mauryan Empire.txt; NCERT/R.S. Sharma and Upinder Singh standard treatment; Mauryan PYQ bank (.research/pyq-bank/hist-ancient-mauryan.md)

items.front: Into how many broad divisions are the Arthashastra’s 15 books and 180 chapters grouped?
items.back: 3 broad divisions.

items.front: Under which king did Kautilya continue as prime minister after Chandragupta?

items.back: The state has seven limbs: king, minister, territory, fort, treasury, army and ally.

items.front: Who were the Sthanikas?

items.front: What was a Rashtrapala?

items.front: What was the role of the Mauryan state in the economy?
items.back: The state controlled all economic activities.

items.front: What did the Mauryan state do to raise farm output?
